key_insight: Moist convection produces height- and scale-dependent energy transfers, including an inverse potential-energy cascade above cloud base and renewed forward transfers in the upper cloud layer.
engineering_relevance: These findings can inform turbulence closures for cloud-resolving and weather models by highlighting phase-change forcing and transport effects absent from standard cascade assumptions.
method: Large Eddy Simulation of BOMEX trade-wind cumulus at 10 m grid resolution.
Anelastic dynamics with moist thermodynamics and phase changes.
Scale-by-scale velocity and buoyancy structure-function budgets to diagnose kinetic- and potential-energy transfers.
evidence_signal: The simulation identifies four dynamical regions, and 1D horizontal subsamples agree well with recent airborne measurements.
watch_item: Results come from one simulated trade-wind cumulus case, so generalization to other cloud regimes and unresolved scales requires further testing.
paper_title: Energy cascades in atmospheric moist convection
